case_title: Achhar Singh v. State of Himachal Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour; prior enmity/dispute (alleged land dispute, prior litigation and social boycott of the complainant's family)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.452 (Budhi Singh); IPC s.452, s.326, s.323 (Achhar Singh)
weapon: Axe (used by both appellants); other accused had sickles, spears and sticks
evidence_type: Eyewitness; medical (post-mortem and injury evidence); recovery (axe and house articles); FIR
aggravating_circumstances: Axe blow to the head of an elderly victim, with knowledge that it would in all probability cause death
trial_court_outcome: All accused acquitted by Additional Sessions Judge, Mandi, giving benefit of doubt (24.02.1998)
high_court_outcome: Acquittal of the two appellants set aside; Budhi Singh convicted under ss.302 and 452 IPC (life imprisonment with fine); Achhar Singh convicted under ss.452, 326 and 323 IPC (five years RI with fine); acquittal of the other five accused upheld
offence_finally_established: Budhi Singh: IPC s.302 (murder) and s.452 (house trespass). Achhar Singh: IPC s.452, s.326 (grievous hurt by dangerous weapon) and s.323 (hurt).
neutral_facts: On a night in February, the complainant's family had returned home from a wedding function in a nearby village with food. At about 8 pm, while the family was eating, a group of villagers came to the house, shouted for the complainant and his father to come out, and began pelting stones. The family retreated and bolted the door, but the group broke it open and entered the house armed with axes, sickles, spears and sticks. It is alleged that one accused struck an elderly relative of the complainant on the head with an axe, causing death on the spot, and that another accused struck the complainant's father with an axe, causing him to faint. Other assailants beat the complainant with sticks, and he escaped to the roof. Some bystanders intervened and the attackers left. The complainant walked through the night to the police station and lodged a First Information Report the next morning. Police recovered sticks, a blood-stained stone, glass splinters, pieces of wood, broken door pieces, a broken bulb and blood-stained soil from the house, and an axe from one accused. Blood marks were also found on a path outside the house. The post-mortem found one fatal sharp-edged head injury, which the doctor said could have been caused by the recovered axe. The injured man had incised wounds on the face and back of the skull and a facial bone fracture, which the doctor said could be caused by an axe. The complainant, his wife and his father gave consistent eyewitness accounts of the attack.
physical_harm: Death of the elderly victim from a single fatal sharp-edged head injury (axe); injured male with incised wounds on face and posterior skull, facial bone fracture, and other grievous and simple injuries
number_of_offences: 7 charged (IPC ss.147, 148, 452, 506, 323, 302, 326, framed against the accused persons collectively); 4 finally upheld (IPC ss.302, 452, 326, 323 across the two appellants)
financial_property_loss: Property damage to the house (broken door, windows, utensils); no monetary value stated
premeditation_planning: Not stated. The High Court noted no common intention to kill was suggested; premeditation was not addressed.
motive: alleged: land dispute (purchase of the complainant's land) and prior litigation; social boycott of the complainant's family
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent eyewitness testimony (P.W.1, P.W.11, P.W.12) that the appellant Budhi Singh gave the fatal axe blow and Achhar Singh attacked with an axe; post-mortem report; doctor's testimony; axe recovery; recoveries from the house corroborated by P.W.14 and P.W.16
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses exaggerated but their core account was consistent and matched the medical evidence; exaggerations were separable from truth; no reason shown to falsely implicate; trial court erred in discarding the evidence
bail_history: Bail bonds cancelled by the Supreme Court; grant of bail earlier not described
trial_duration: offence: 23.02.1996; trial judgment: 24.02.1998; High Court: 12.05.2010 and 27.05.2010; Supreme Court: 07.05.2021
legal_representation: Appellants: J.S. Attri and R. Basant (Senior Advocates) with others. State: Abhinav Mukerji, AAG.
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; charge-sheet filed against seven persons; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: None noted by the Supreme Court (the High Court considered and explained the delay in lodging the FIR)
appeal_history: Trial court: all acquitted (24.02.1998). High Court: acquittal of two appellants set aside and convictions recorded; acquittal of the other five upheld. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed, High Court convictions maintained.
prosecution_argument: Relying on Sheikh Hasib and Dharma Rama Bhagare, the FIR is not substantive evidence; witnesses' credibility is not affected by relationship or minor discrepancies or exaggerations (Kishan Chand, Leela Ram); inconsistent evidence against one accused cannot benefit another (Gangadhar Behera, Prabhu Dayal)
defence_argument: Trial court's view was a possible view and interference required perversity (Murugesan, Aruvelu); witnesses exaggerated and falsely implicated; medical evidence showed only one head injury; axe recovered from public place; blood trail outside the house; police arrival timing; no reason for the appellant to attack neighbours on his daughter's wedding day
legal_principle_applied: Presumption of innocence is doubled after acquittal; appellate courts show self-restraint and interfere only for perversity, but the High Court may re-appreciate evidence fully; exaggeration must be separated from falsity; benefit of doubt only where a firm conclusion cannot be reached
precedent_relied_upon: Chandrappa v. State of Karnataka (2007) 4 SCC 415; State of AP v. M. Madhusudhan Rao (2008) 15 SCC 582; Raveen Kumar v. State of HP 2020 SCC OnLine SC 869; Murugesan v. State (2012) 10 SCC 383; Aruvelu v. State (2009) 10 SCC 206; Hari Chand v. State of Delhi (1996) 9 SCC 112; Sucha Singh v. State of Punjab (2003) 7 SCC 643; Babu v. State of Kerala (2010) 9 SCC 189; Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1953 SC 364; Sarwan Singh v. State of Punjab (1976) 4 SCC 369
judicial_aggravating_factors: Axe blow to the head of an elderly victim, with knowledge that it would in all probability cause death
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds cancelled; appellants directed to undergo the remainder of their sentence
